newsitem.title: FRANCE: No Suez merger plan with Gen de Belgique - chairman.
newsitem.headline: No Suez merger plan with Gen de Belgique - chairman.

text.p: French holding company Compagnie Financiere de Suez has no intention of merging with its holding subsidiary Societe Generale de Belgique, chairman Gerard Mestrallet told the Financial Times.

"SGB's costs are less than 0.3 percent of assets it manages. It offers good value for money," Mestrallet said in an interview, reacting to stock market speculation he might absorb the unit as part of his streamlining efforts.
He said SGB was a handy vehicle to buy Belgian assets, such as Tractebel and Generale de Banque Generale Bank without poltical objections against a foreign buyer.
Mestrallet was also reported as welcoming the arrival of Belgian businessman Albert Frere in the share capital and he "hopes to see him on the board soon", the paper said.
Mestrallet said he was trying to make the company more focused.
"Our strategy was not visible in the past, but I think little by little it will become clear and well-defined," he was quoted as saying.
